name: Tooltip
intent: Brief label or hint shown on hover/focus to name an icon or clarify a terse control.
when: An icon-only button needs a name
A truncated or terse control needs a short explanation

chooseOver.because: HoverCard is for richer preview content; Tooltip is a short text label
Popover holds interactive content on click; Tooltip is non-interactive hover text

commonMistakes.mistake: Put interactive content in a tooltip
commonMistakes.fix: Use Popover or HoverCard (see fm-prim-2 for the TooltipProvider rule)
commonMistakes.avoidOverride: Put interactive content in a tooltip — use Popover or HoverCard (see fm-prim-2 for the TooltipProvider rule)

usage: Use Tooltip when you need to display content that temporarily overlays the main interface. This component is useful for focused interactions, confirmations, or supplementary information.
Tooltip should be used sparingly as overlays interrupt the user's workflow. Reserve this component for important interactions that require user attention or action before continuing.

anatomy.description: Tooltip is composed of the following parts:

bestPractices.title: Keep content brief
bestPractices.description: Use short, helpful text that adds context.

bestPractices.title: Don't overload with content
bestPractices.description: Avoid putting long text or complex UI in tooltips.
bestPractices.example: <Tooltip content="This is a very long explanation...">

bestPractices.title: Ensure accessibility
bestPractices.description: Make tooltip content available to screen readers.

bestPractices.title: Don't hide critical info
bestPractices.description: Never put essential information only in tooltips.
bestPractices.example: // Required field indicator only in tooltip

bestPractices.title: Use appropriate triggers
bestPractices.description: Show on hover for mouse, focus for keyboard users.

bestPractices.title: Don't require click to view
bestPractices.description: Avoid click-to-open tooltips that hide quick information.
